papers.title: Topographical Patterns of Slow Wave Activity in Sleep Talking: An Exploratory Polysomnographic Investigation.
papers.summary: Compared overnight polysomnographic slow-wave activity (SWA) topography in 12 young sleep talkers versus 10 matched controls. Sleep talkers showed a stable central SWA increase across sleep stages and a frontopolar SWA decrease primarily in N2 sleep, suggesting local, frequency-specific (≥1 Hz) SWA regulation.

papers.title: The mTOR pathway drives daily physiology
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that mTOR is a major clock output pathway required for most daily variation in mammalian physiology, with PERIOD2 interacting directly with mTORC1. Acute mTOR inhibition abolishes functional rhythms in cells and most daily liver physiology, while preserving sleep/wake cycles, and shows evolutionary conservation as a circadian effector across species.

papers.title: Circadian photoreceptor CRYPTOCHROME promotes wakefulness under short winter-like days via a GABAergic circuitry.
papers.summary: The study shows that loss of the circadian photoreceptor cryptochrome (cry) in Drosophila increases sleep under short winter-like days, mimicking seasonal affective disorder hypersomnolence. CRY functions in GABAergic neurons, including small ventral lateral neurons, to downregulate GABAergic tone, thereby enhancing activity of wake-promoting large ventral lateral neurons under short-day conditions.

papers.title: Reactivation of neural signatures of food during REM-like sleep in the high-level visual cortex of monkeys
papers.summary: Wireless neural recordings in high-level visual (IT) and motor regions of two monkeys while awake viewing food, faces, and objects, and during natural sleep. Decoders trained to categorize food responses showed increased probability during REM-like sleep compared with NREM or wake, indicating selective reactivation of behaviorally relevant visual stimuli.

papers.title: Recurrent Sleep Restriction During Aging Induces Early Recognition Memory Impairment, Neuroinflammation, and Blood-Brain Barrier Dysfunction in Female Wistar Rats.
papers.summary: Recurrent sleep restriction in aging female Wistar rats increased blood-brain barrier permeability, hippocampal TNF-α and IL-1β, and accelerated recognition memory decline. A single sleep restriction episode impaired recognition memory, while senescence markers showed age- and region-dependent changes without a clear effect of recurrent sleep restriction.

papers.title: Daily experiences affect the timing rather than the structure of sleep.
papers.journal: Annals of behavioral medicine : a publication of the Society of Behavioral Medicine
papers.summary: Using multiday mobile EEG and daily diaries in 1901 nights, the study found that daily experiences primarily affect sleep timing rather than sleep structure. After accounting for extended wakefulness, only four effects survived correction: longer sleep and N3 after workplace days, increased REM latency after social activity, and reduced sleep onset latency after alcohol consumption.

papers.title: The Neurochemical Basis of High-Altitude Sleep Disruption: Disentangling Respiratory and Sleep-Circuit Mechanisms Toward Targeted Pharmacotherapy.
papers.summary: Reviews the neurochemical basis of high-altitude sleep disruption, using a randomized controlled trial where acetazolamide reduced AHI and improved oxygenation but did not restore N3 slow-wave sleep or sleep efficiency. Proposes a dual-target framework involving serotonergic, adenosinergic, orexin/hypocretin, and locus coeruleus norepinephrine nodes plus HIF-1α.

papers.title: Spontaneous slow waves index multiple dimensions of recovery in Disorders of Consciousness
papers.summary: In 236 DoC patients, higher-amplitude and steeper spontaneous slow waves indexed greater consciousness and better one-year recovery, with slow-wave features above-chance classification of MCS- and MCS+ versus UWS and structural associations to subcortico-cortical projection integrity.

papers.title: Multimodal LLMs Can Learn to Read Brain Signals: A Vision--Language Model for Unified Multi-Task EEG Decoding
papers.summary: BraVista, a vision-language framework encoding multichannel EEG as structured images and instruction-conditioned tuning of a general-domain VLM, achieved strong multi-task performance across sleep staging, emotion recognition, cognitive workload, and abnormal EEG detection, with EEG-to-image representation critical and gradual degradation under noise.

papers.title: REM sleep infraslow rhythms correlate with neuropsychiatric symptom severity
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional polysomnographic study of 59 male veterans, REM infraslow rhythms in respiratory rate, but not cardiac rate or EEG beta power, correlated with neuropsychiatric symptom severity including PTSD, pain, anxiety, depression, and cognitive difficulties. Conventional REM metrics showed no significant correlations; eye movements preferentially occurred during high respiratory rate, low beta power, and intermediate cardiac rate periods.

papers.title: Circadian misalignment and low-grade inflammation: Failure of temporal gating by the molecular clock.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes molecular, animal, and human evidence to propose that circadian misalignment impairs temporal gating of innate immunity by the molecular clock, particularly via REV-ERBα and BMAL1 regulation of NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome. It highlights that controlled human protocols show modest increases in 24-hour high-sensitivity C-reactive protein even when sleep loss is controlled, but causal inference remains incomplete.

papers.title: Effects of Gallic Acid on Sleep and Circadian Rhythm in a Drosophila melanogaster Model of Fragile X Syndrome: An Integrative Behavioral and Bioinformatic Approach for Target Predictions.
papers.journal: The Yale journal of biology and medicine
papers.summary: Assessed gallic acid effects on sleep and circadian rhythm in a Drosophila model of fragile X syndrome across seven concentrations using video monitoring. Gallic acid altered sleep and circadian parameters in a concentration-dependent manner, most pronounced at lower concentrations, with bioinformatic predictions implicating Rac1, bsk, Jra, Cyfip, and Dscam1.

papers.title: The Case for Kinases: a Phosphorylation Driven Model for Circadian Temperature Compensation in Neurospora crassa.
papers.summary: Using novel alleles and quantitative proteomics, this study investigated the genetic relationship between Casein Kinase I (CK-1a) and Casein Kinase II (CKA) in regulating temperature compensation of the Neurospora circadian clock. The results support a phosphorylation-driven model in which decreasing CK1 activity on FRQ with increasing temperature is countered by increasing CK2 activity, shaping the FRQ phosphorylation landscape to maintain period length.

papers.title: From retina to brain: retinal dysfunction and dopaminergic neurodegeneration in Drosophila models of Parkinson's disease.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Using Drosophila models of Parkinson's disease, the study examined effects of parkin silencing and human α-Synuclein expression on photoreceptor morphology and function, and assessed sleep patterns and dopaminergic neuron degeneration in the PAM cluster. The findings highlight the interplay between retinal dysfunction and dopaminergic neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Longitudinal associations of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and slow-wave sleep with plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: Longitudinally examined associations of REM sleep and slow-wave sleep with plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers in 64 cognitively unimpaired older adults over 2.6 years. Frontal slow-wave activity was cross-sectionally associated with plasma Aβ42/40, whereas low REM sleep percentage predicted faster annualized decline in Aβ42/40, especially in amyloid-positive participants.

papers.title: Development of Rest-Activity Rhythms in Infancy and Their Disruption in Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The study characterized rest-activity rhythm (RAR) maturation in healthy infants and compared RARs in infants with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) to age-matched controls. In 891 actigraphy recordings from 333 healthy infants, RAR height, interdaily stability, entropy, and fractal complexity increased with age while fragmentation decreased; infants with IESS (n=11) showed marked reductions in RAR height, interdaily stability, entropy, and fractal complexity compared to controls.

papers.title: Modulation of circadian rhythms in articular cartilage by heat pulse.
papers.summary: This study tested whether heat pulses can resynchronize dampened circadian rhythms in articular cartilage using PER2::LUC reporter mice. A 60-min 43°C heat pulse resynchronized rhythms in young and aged cartilage, counteracted IL-1α-induced disruption, and required HSP90 and actin/Rho-ROCK signaling.

papers.title: High-frequency oscillations arise through distinct mechanisms in models of α- synucleinopathy and channelopathy-induced epilepsy.
papers.summary: The study quantified cortical high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, 250-500 Hz) and interictal spikes in a transgenic α-synucleinopathy model (A53T mice, a model of dementia with Lewy bodies) and a channelopathy-induced epilepsy model (Kcna1-/- mice). Both models showed elevated HFOs across vigilance states, but A53T mice had more HFOs and interictal spikes, with higher frequency and longer duration HFOs, and HFOs were most prevalent during non-REM sleep in A53T mice, suggesting distinct mechanisms.

papers.title: Quarterly Sleep-Pain Coupling in Knee Pain: Pain-to-Sleep Dominance, Localization Dependence, and Reward-Circuit Moderation of Sleep-to-Pain Coupling.
papers.summary: This study investigated quarterly sleep-pain coupling over three years in 229 adults with knee pain using Bayesian bivariate autoregression. Pain-to-sleep coupling was credible but sleep-to-pain coupling was not, and the latter was moderated by baseline pain-evoked deactivation in the nucleus accumbens and anterior cingulate cortex.

papers.title: Deciphering the heterogeneity of prodromal α-synucleinopathy: linking brain biotyping and gut dysbiosis in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.summary: This study examined gut microbiome and brain structure associations in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) biotypes using shotgun metagenomics and neuroimaging in 167 participants. Both biotypes showed depletion of short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria, but Biotype 1 had more pronounced taxonomic alterations associated with specific brain atrophy.

papers.title: Music-evoked EEG signals for mental health assessment using two- and three-class classification.
papers.summary: This preliminary study used EEG recordings from 48 participants during music and no-music sessions with mental health questionnaires to classify mental fatigue and multi-output anxiety, depression, and stress using a deep residual MLP. Binary classification achieved 72.92% accuracy in the music condition vs 58.33% without music, with 96.67% recall in music; multi-output classification showed 93.75% accuracy for stress but low AUC (35.56%), and anxiety and depression were harder to classify.

papers.title: Which cognitive emotion-regulation strategies are implicated in the association between sleep quality and negative affect?
papers.summary: This preregistered cross-sectional study examined cognitive emotion regulation as a mediator between sleep quality and negative affect in 899 adults. Poorer sleep quality was associated with greater negative affect, with indirect effects through maladaptive regulation strategies such as self-blame, rumination, and catastrophizing.

papers.title: Associations of Sleep Duration and Adherence to Age-Specific Sleep Recommendations with Body Fat and Related Anthropometric Characteristics in Children and Adolescents.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 1402 children and adolescents aged 3-16 years in Kraków examined associations between parent-reported sleep duration, adherence to age-specific sleep recommendations, and detailed anthropometric adiposity measures. Longer sleep duration was consistently but modestly associated with lower body mass, BMI, adiposity, circumferences, and waist-to-height ratio; adherence to sleep recommendations was not independently associated with adiposity after adjustment for age.

papers.title: A Cortical Stress Signature of Fear-Induced Walking: Mobile Electroencephalography Theta Suppression in Older Women With Fear of Falling.
papers.journal: Psychogeriatrics : the official journal of the Japanese Psychogeriatric Society
papers.summary: This within-subject study used mobile EEG to examine cortical oscillatory activity during walking under a fear-of-falling stressor in 30 older women. The stressor reduced relative theta power across multiple brain regions and decreased the frontal and central theta/beta ratio, providing a cortical signature of fear-induced walking.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation, tolerability, and the Alpha/Theta EEG ratio: a controlled pilot study relevant to emotion regulation.
papers.summary: This controlled pilot randomized ten healthy women to eight sessions of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) or waitlist control and found that between-group changes in Alpha/Theta and Theta/Beta EEG ratios favored taVNS (both U=25, exact p=.008) after FDR correction, with 100% protocol completion and no serious adverse events under individually titrated stimulation (14–25 mA). Within-group changes in the taVNS group were not significant and stimulation intensity showed no positive dose-response.

papers.title: A comparative study and analysis of recent EEG-based brain-computer interface approaches and their applications.
papers.summary: This review compares recent EEG-based brain-computer interface approaches and applications, including feature extraction, classification, and connectivity analysis. It reports that among deep learning models, ATCNet achieved the highest accuracy (86.46%) while EEG-TCNet had the lowest (50.69%).

papers.title: Rev-erb-α in Skeletal Muscle Adaptation: Integrating Circadian Control Mechanisms and Exercise Dynamic Responses.
papers.summary: This review consolidates experimental evidence on the role of Rev-erb-α in skeletal muscle adaptation to exercise, highlighting its circadian regulation and pleiotropic actions. It reports that exercise induces bimodal Rev-erb-α regulation, with downregulation immediately post-exercise followed by an increase, and that higher physical activity increases its 24-hour amplitude.

papers.title: Night-shift work is associated with peripheral clock gene dysregulation and circadian transcriptional network remodeling in female healthcare workers.
papers.summary: This study experimentally validated a circadian gene panel and investigated YY1 in 93 female healthcare workers, finding that night-shift workers showed significantly lower expression of CLOCK, TEF, PER1, and YY1 compared to day-shift workers. A four-gene model discriminated groups with AUC 0.940, improved to 0.976 with YY1.

papers.title: Toward Personalized Surgeons' Cognitive Workload: A Linear Mixed-Effects Model Analysis of EEG Features.
papers.summary: This study used a linear mixed-effects model framework to analyze EEG features from nine surgical trainees during simulated microvascular anastomosis with six surgical flow disruptions, finding that theta and beta power bands were significantly affected across the group, while a subjectivity index identified features such as Gamma Asymmetry with high individualization despite no significant group trend. Features with both significant fixed effects and high subjectivity indices, such as Mean Power Beta, were identified as the most reliable metrics for tracking cognitive load.

papers.title: Prevalence of adult attention-deficit/ hyperactivity disorder symptoms among university students and their relation to sleeping duration, time management skills, and academic performance.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study estimated the prevalence of adult ADHD symptoms among 612 university students in Saudi Arabia and examined associations with sleep duration, time management, and academic performance. It found a 26% prevalence of ADHD symptoms, with significant associations with female sex (OR=1.58), sleeping fewer than 4 hours per night (OR=2.46), and lower GPA (OR=2.10).

papers.title: A Qualitative Exploration of Barriers and Facilitators to Changing Provider's Current Evaluation and Treatment Decision-Making for Velopharyngeal Insufficiency.
papers.journal: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
papers.summary: This qualitative study interviewed 28 surgeons and 16 speech-language pathologists from 12 cleft teams to identify barriers and facilitators to changing evaluation and treatment decision-making for velopharyngeal insufficiency. Providers required evidence of improved speech outcomes or reduced obstructive sleep apnea risk, and favored applying new approaches to complex cases or defined subgroups rather than broad adoption.

papers.title: The contribution of circadian, sleep and hormonal rhythms to pregnancy outcomes: an opportunity for improved management of women during pregnancy.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence linking circadian and sleep disruption to adverse pregnancy outcomes, focusing on temporal regulation of hormones including progesterone, estrogen, cortisol, oxytocin, and melatonin. It highlights emerging mechanistic insights into molecular clock regulation in reproductive tissues and proposes chronobiology-informed diagnostics and chronotherapeutic strategies for improving pregnancy management.

papers.title: Respiratory function, functional capacity, dyspnea, and sleep quality in young adults using the IQOS heated tobacco product: a matched cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This matched cross-sectional study found that young exclusive IQOS users had shorter 6-minute walk test distances, higher dyspnea scores, and poorer sleep quality compared to matched never-tobacco users, despite similar resting spirometry. Maximal inspiratory pressure tended to be lower in IQOS users but was not statistically significant.

papers.title: Patient and caregiver burden after hospitalization with severe viral lower respiratory tract disease: results from a real-world survey in Europe, the US and Japan.
papers.summary: A real-world cross-sectional survey of 1071 patients hospitalized with severe viral lower respiratory tract disease 6-24 months prior and 104 caregivers across Europe, the US, and Japan found persistent physical and mental health burdens, with 66% of patients reporting mental health impact and 50% of caregivers reporting moderate-to-extreme sleep impact. Mean EQ-5D-5L was 0.72 and caregiver Zarit Burden Interview score was 15.0, indicating notable post-discharge quality-of-life and productivity impairments.

papers.title: Maternal Circadian Preference is Associated With Cardiorespiratory Fitness and Participation in Structured Prenatal Exercise.
papers.summary: In pregnant women from two randomized controlled exercise trials, greater evening chronotype was associated with lower cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2peak) and significantly lower compliance with a structured prenatal exercise program. Exploratory analyses found a significant Time × Chronotype interaction for HDL cholesterol, which increased from 16 to 36 weeks' gestation in morning-oriented women but did not change in evening-oriented women.

papers.title: Lay cousellor-delivered wisdom-enhancement narrative-therapy and empathy-focused interventions to reduce loneliness among older adults: A three-arm randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a three-arm randomized controlled trial with 287 older adults, telephone-based wisdom-enhancement narrative therapy (Tele-NT) significantly reduced overall loneliness on the De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale at 6 and 12 months compared to an active control group. Tele-NT also reduced emotional and social loneliness and improved sleep quality at 12 months.

papers.title: Appropriateness/inappropriateness of access to an in-hospital rehabilitation program for patients with respiratory disease.
papers.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
papers.summary: Analysis of 10 years of hospitalization records from seven Italian rehabilitation centers found high overall appropriateness (73-87% across items) for in-hospital respiratory rehabilitation admissions, with only 2.8% deemed inappropriate. Chronic respiratory failure patients had the highest appropriateness (>78% across items) and the lowest inappropriateness (0.7%), while dyspnea and OSAS subgroups had lower appropriateness.

papers.title: Hyperactive Delirium Temporally Associated With Hydroxyzine in a Child With Succinic Semialdehyde Dehydrogenase Deficiency Presenting With Psychotic Symptoms: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 12-year-old girl with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD) who presented with psychotic symptoms and developed hyperactive delirium temporally associated with hydroxyzine exposure, which was discontinued. Low-dose quetiapine and environmental interventions led to improvement in sleep, appetite, and behavioral regulation.

papers.title: Integrated analysis uncovers the role of circadian rhythm genes in cold adaptation of Kandelia obovata using the multi-omics data.
papers.summary: The study assembled a chromosome-level genome of Kandelia candel and integrated comparative genomics, population resequencing, transcriptomics, and metabolomics to identify circadian rhythm-related transcription factors associated with cold adaptation in the mangrove Kandelia obovata. It prioritized 18 candidate circadian TFs, including PIF3, CCA1, LHY, and MYB members such as PAP1, and highlighted flavonoid and phenylpropanoid metabolism as downstream pathways potentially contributing to cold tolerance.

papers.title: Case Report: Rapid resolution of psychogenic cough in an adolescent following bromazepam treatment.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 13-year-old male with severe somatic cough syndrome (psychogenic cough) that resolved completely within 24-36 hours after short-term bromazepam treatment. At 3-month follow-up, the patient remained symptom-free without medication, suggesting benzodiazepines may be an alternative when behavioral therapy is unavailable.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
